source_text: Cum igitur liquido clareat hanc sanam et veram esse sententiam, quam primo loco ratio, deinde Scripturarum munivit auctoritas, et quam sanctorum virorum semper celebravit eruditio, qui tamen veritati auctoritatem non suo tribuere consensu, sed testimonium et gloriam de eius suscepere consortium, nullum prudentum conturbet conspiratio perditorum
pass_a_gloss: When/with therefore clearly it-is-clear this sound and true to-be position, than/which first loco reason, then of-the-Scriptures fortified authority, and than/which sanctorum virorum always has-celebrated learning, who nevertheless veritati auctoritatem not his-own to-grant by-agreement, but testimony and gloriam about/from his/its they-received sharing, no of-prudent-ones let-disturb conspiracy of-the-lost.
pass_b_english: Since it is plainly clear that this is the sound and true position, supported first by reason and then by the authority of Scripture, and always upheld by the learning of holy men—who did not give truth its authority by agreeing with it, but received a good testimony and glory from sharing in it—let no prudent person be disturbed by a conspiracy of the lost.

choices.why: Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
